newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 5.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - An unusually large portion of 1996 bank audits will be undertaken by the six largest international auditing firms. Many of the banks made the decision to go with an international auditor by themselves, while a number were referred by the Czech National Bank.
- The government has approved a proposal to protect the Czech market from imports being sold at dumping prices, which are at least two percent lower than in the country the product is imported from.

- A devaluation or depreciation of the crown will not solve the problem of the trade deficit, according to the vice-governer of the Czech National Bank, Pavel Kysilka. While such steps would help exporters increase their price competitiveness, the real source of the deficit is high imports.
- New customs tarrifs were approved by the government yesterday, according to Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik. There are 7,000 changes to the tarrifs for 1997.
- The supervisory board of Ceska Pojistovna has approved a decision by its board to pay back depositary certificates from the bankrupt Kreditni Banka.
- Skodaexport Praha a.s., one of the strongest Czech foreign trade companies, is expecting a turnover of approximately seven billion crowns in 1996., according to the company's manager, Zdenek Sima.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Motoinvest and 1. CS Holding would like to see the 400 million crowns they provided Agrobanka with returned. Agrobanka was to use the funds to raise its basic capital, but was put under forced administration, and the current administrator has refused all of Motoinvest's requests.
- While tourism is expected to add a record $4 billion to the state's coffers, even this will not help to decrease the balance of payments.
PRAVO - Selling the five percent share Ceska Posta has in Investicni a Postovni Banka could be risky, according to a press spokesman for the bank, Jan Rezek.
